name: Vanuatu water drumming and sand drawing
lineage: Vanuatu water drumming tradition of the Ranmwat Bay and Hog Harbour communities of north-central Espiritu Santo island, in which women stand thigh-deep in the sea or in a freshwater pool and strike the water surface with cupped hands producing distinctive low-pitched rhythmic-percussive patterns. Performance contexts span entertainment, ceremonial-celebration, and tourism-circuit demonstrations. Parallel to the water-drumming, Vanuatu preserves the canonical sand-drawing tradition in which elaborate diagrammatic geometric-and-mythological drawings are produced in sand with continuous-line technique. Distinguished from neighboring Melanesian water-percussion variants by Vanuatu-specific Ranmwat-Hog-Harbour stylistic conventions.
